slot.brief: Mix volumes of two solutions (an acid and a base of unequal basicity) and compute the molarity of the excess species left in the final mixture.

stem: On mixing $100\ \text{mL}$ of $0.10\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ with $200\ \text{mL}$ of $0.20\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ $\text{NaOH}$, what is the molarity of excess $\text{OH}^-$? Assume complete neutralisation.
working:
$n(\text{OH}^-)=0.200(0.20)=0.040\ \text{mol}$
$n(\text{OH}^-)_{\text{required}}=3(0.100)(0.10)=0.030\ \text{mol}$
$[\text{OH}^-]_{\text{excess}}=\dfrac{0.040-0.030}{0.300}=3.33\times10^{-2}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$

Independent check: H₃PO₄ = 0.100×0.10 = 0.010 mol, requiring 3×0.010 = 0.030 mol OH⁻. Excess OH⁻ = 0.040−0.030 = 0.010 mol; total volume = 0.300 L, so [OH⁻] = 0.010/0.300 = 3.33×10⁻² mol L⁻¹.
solution:
Complete neutralisation of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ requires $3$ mol of $\text{OH}^-$ per mole of acid.
$$n_{\text{OH}^-\!,\,\text{excess}}=(0.200)(0.20)-3(0.100)(0.10)=0.010\ \text{mol}$$
The total volume is $0.300\ \text{L}$, so $[\text{OH}^-]=0.010/0.300=3.33\times10^{-2}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$.
